resource_boundaries.description: Portable Python semantics should not silently depend on CPython implementation notes; implementation-specific behavior is isolated under profile.cpython-resource-limits.
The local CPython 3.14.6 build records optional extension availability as environment-dependent, excluded conformance inputs rather than portable language semantics.
CPython sys.getrecursionlimit and sys.setrecursionlimit behavior, including current-depth checks and RecursionError boundaries, is not modeled by the current K runtime.
CPython's integer string conversion length limit, sys.get_int_max_str_digits, sys.set_int_max_str_digits, -X int_max_str_digits, and PYTHONINTMAXSTRDIGITS are not modeled by the current K runtime.
The Unix resource module and process resource-limit APIs are platform behavior outside the current portable Python semantics.

known_gaps: No recursion-depth cell or RecursionError threshold is modeled.
No CPython integer string conversion length limit is enforced.
No process, stack, CPU, memory, file descriptor, locale, terminal, or optional-extension availability profile is modeled.
No command-line -X option or environment-variable profile is modeled.
Current executable semantics should treat these as CPython/environment profile work rather than portable language behavior.
